node.data: Who authored the deployment that triggered INC-003?

[{"decision": "Trace INC-003 to every triggering deployment, then to each author.", "tool": "graph-traversal", "obs": "Auth Service v2.1 --[TRIGGERED]--> INC-003; Auth Service v2.1 --[AUTHORED_BY]--> Alice; API Gateway v3.2.1 --[TRIGGERED]--> INC-003; API Gateway v3.2.1 --[AUTHORED_BY]--> David."}]
INC-003 was triggered by Auth Service v2.1, authored by Alice of the Identity Team, and API Gateway v3.2.1, authored by David of the Platform Team.

[{"decision": "Use the incident record and resolver relationships to reconstruct both rollback actions.", "tool": "graph-traversal", "obs": "INC-003 --[RESOLVED_BY]--> Omar; INC-003 --[RESOLVED_BY]--> Sara. The incident record says Omar rolled Auth Service v2.1 back to v2.0.3, Sara reverted the API Gateway routing update, and cache-flush propagation completed."}]

INC-003 was resolved by two coordinated rollbacks: Omar from the Identity Team rolled Auth Service v2.1 back to v2.0.3, restoring stable token validation, and Sara from the Platform Team reverted the API Gateway routing update. The system stabilized after the rollbacks and cache-flush propagation completed.
How do I fix the API Gateway after a bad deployment?

[{"decision": "Use the API Gateway remediation runbook.", "tool": "runbook-lookup", "obs": "Owner: Platform Team. Check Gateway error rate; inspect recent routing changes; run kubectl rollout undo deploy/api-gateway; page Platform Team on-call."}]
Check the Gateway error rate in Grafana, inspect recent routing changes, run kubectl rollout undo deploy/api-gateway, and page the Platform Team on-call.
Which services were affected when INC-003 occurred?
[{"decision": "Traverse every AFFECTS edge from INC-003.", "tool": "graph-traversal", "obs": "INC-003 --[AFFECTS]--> Auth Service, API Gateway, Cache Service, Database Service."}]
INC-003 affected Auth Service, API Gateway, Cache Service, and Database Service.
